sources.fact: Every few hours one side of the nose becomes more congested and the other decongests (nasal cycle); turbinate blood vessels swell and shrink alternately; you shouldn't notice it; see a healthcare provider if a stuffy nose isn't going away or is getting worse

Kahana-Zweig et al. 2016, PLoS ONE: greater-airflow nostril shifts between left and right; cycle about 2 hours awake, longer in sleep; all 33 subjects cycled; engorgement of erectile tissue from asymmetric blood flow; proposed roles include air conditioning and optimising each nostril for different odors (theory)
Nasal cycle: mean about 2.5 hours, varies widely; keeps one side of the nose moist for humidification; people usually don't notice; each nostril may detect a different range of smells

math.note: Kahana-Zweig et al. 2016: 33 subjects, all cycled

post.instagram_caption:
One of your nostrils is slacking off right now 👃

It's called the nasal cycle. Blood vessels inside one side of your nose swell so it lets less air through, and every few hours the sides swap. In one study, all 33 people tested were cycling, and most of us never notice.

Scientists think it may help keep the nose from drying out, and each side may smell things a little differently. If one side stays blocked and won't clear, see a doctor.

Sources: Cleveland Clinic, PLoS ONE (Kahana-Zweig et al. 2016), Wikipedia.
